title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
On Aug. 3 in a Cypress neighborhood, Harris County sheriff’s deputies surrounded a Camaro driven by two 19-year-olds, Anthony and Julian, after flock cameras flagged a stolen Camaro linked to several aggravated robberies. At least five patrol cars and a helicopter responded because deputies could not read the license plate. Deputies drew guns, ordered the men to the ground, and handcuffed them. Julian says a deputy shoved him, causing cuts and scrapes, and threatened to shoot and kill him. Only after the men were handcuffed did deputies realize they had stopped the wrong car. The men were not charged.

Anthony’s mother, Leslie, plans to hire an attorney and believes deputies could have run the plates or used a normal traffic stop. The sheriff’s office says supervisors, including the district captain and shift lieutenants, will review body camera footage to check that procedures were followed. The two men were given information on how to file a formal complaint with internal affairs, and both plan to do so.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
